new: Back into the cell's Network tab can save the network on show for wwiznet, the Menche lab's 3D network explorer: Export for wwiznet (ZIP) gives every protein in each of its places at its place in the cell, the links with their verdicts, a ready view and a guide window. Also from the command line (packages/ppicell/README.md). The same tab opens a wwiznet dataset (its edges.tsv, with its nodes.tsv or its folder) as your own network, reading only the links, a score, a kind and the protein names.

Still untried: v210's two voices, v209's shared networks, v208's sharing with a room, v207's Network tab, v206 lining up a worn character, v205 sides and complexes, v204 to v200 (mirror robot, tour tables, sharp VR text, any mix of devices).
test: On a laptop: Back into the cell, explore, Network tab, Export for wwiznet. Unzip into a wwiznet deployment's data folder, add the line from HOW-TO-OPEN.txt, open /?dataset=ppicell. Does the cell read as a cell? Try the guide window's buttons (Impossible only, the hairball, a complex).
Drop a wwiznet dataset's folder (or its edges.tsv and nodes.tsv together) on the Network tab: does it name the proteins by the right column, and can you pick another?
The same dataset in a headset through wwiznet: is it fluid with about 107,000 edges, and is the guide window placed well?
v210 to v200: both voices, sharing a network with a room, the Network tab, lining up a worn character, the mirror robot.
untested: wwiznet drew the export only through its WebGL2 fallback in a headless browser here: never on a real machine with WebGPU, never in a Quest.
Both v210 voices are unheard (pronunciation, pace, level).
v209 and earlier: sharing on the owner's relays, v207's Network tab in a headset and on a phone, v206 with real trackers, v205's rings, v204 to v200 on devices.
